name: PIRM 2018 Challenge on Perceptual Image Super-resolution
description: This paper reports on the 2018 PIRM challenge on perceptual super-resolution (SR), held in conjunction with the Perceptual Image Restoration and Manipulation (PIRM) workshop at ECCV 2018. In contrast to previous SR challenges, our evaluation methodology jointly quantifies accuracy and perceptual quality, therefore enabling perceptual-driven methods to compete alongside algorithms that target PSNR maximization. Twenty-one participating teams introduced algorithms which well-improved upon the existing state-of-the-art methods in perceptual SR, as confirmed by a human opinion study. We also analyze popular image quality measures and draw conclusions regarding which of them correlates best with human opinion scores. We conclude with an analysis of the current trends in perceptual SR, as reflected from the leading submissions.
reputation: A notable ECCV perceptual super-resolution challenge that helped standardize evaluation beyond PSNR by combining fidelity and perceptual quality.
notes: Vision benchmark with human-opinion-based evaluation; results depend on the tradeoff between distortion and perceptual quality and are not directly comparable to PSNR-only SR benchmarks.
